chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Among the first to play Birdland
summary: Machito's orchestra was among the first Latin band at Birdland, played twenty times for Morris Levy, in late 1949 around the Afro-Cuban Suite.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes. All right. Ahh Birdland opened up in 1949. When it opened up, did you get called to play there?
We was one of the first ones.
You were one of the first to play there?
Practically everyone - Power, Bob Power, Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, Lester Young, Gene Ammons, all those guys.
But it - I know Tito Puente played there in 1953. Had you played Birdland before '53.
So then you were the first Latin-American orchestra.
Well, we was at the Birdland so the impact created by the 'Afro-Cuban Suite'....

... so when we were recording - when Bob City or the Birdland was opened, we was involved in Afro-Cuban thing and Morris Levy know us. We know Morris Levy since he was a kid, when he was seventeen or eighteen years old; so they happened to be the owner of the Birdland, so as soon that they opened we played maybe twenty times.
Okay, so then you, the Machito Orchestra, was the first Latin-American orchestra to play Birdland.
I think it was in 1949, late 1949, because the 'Afro-Cuban Suite' was made in the summer.
